 Gold, Silver Rate Today Live Updates: Bullion hovers near one-year low as Fed rate hike bets weigh on prices 
 LIVE NOW Share Comments Gold, Silver Rate Today Live Updates: Bullion hovers near one-year low as Fed rate hike bets weigh on prices
 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Nov 02, 2026, 09:33:25 IST SUMMARY Gold and silver prices are in focus on Monday, November 2, as investors assess the prospects of a recovery after a sharp correction in the precious metals market last week. Gold prices edged higher in early Asian trading but remained close to a one-year low, with inflation concerns and expectations of tighter US monetary policy continuing to weigh on bullion. 
 Spot gold rose 0.5% to $3,894.89 per ounce by 0042 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery gained 0.1% to $3,903.90. Despite the early recovery, prices remained near Friday's level, when gold fell below the key $4,000-per-ounce mark for the first time in more than a year. 
 The latest weakness comes amid growing expectations that the US Federal Reserve could raise interest rates in December to contain persistent inflation. US inflation accelerated in September, with consumers paying more for gasoline and other goods. Three Fed officials also argued for further rate increases on Friday, in the first round of public commentary following last week's monetary policy meeting, at which borrowing costs were left unchanged. 
 Traders are currently pricing in around a 75% chance of a December rate hike, according to the CME FedWatch Tool. Higher interest rates generally weigh on gold because the non-yielding asset becomes less attractive compared with interest-bearing investments. 
 The global sell-off has also affected domestic bullion prices. In New Delhi, gold of 99.9% purity declined by ₹3,200 to ₹1,42,000 per 10 grams on Saturday, while silver fell by ₹4,200 to ₹1,86,000 per kg. Both metals extended their losses for a second consecutive session. 
 The decline in gold has also been linked to a sharp fall in technology stocks, which triggered forced selling of safe-haven assets and margin calls, according to Commerzbank analysts. Meanwhile, physical demand in key Asian markets remained subdued last week. Indian buyers delayed purchases in anticipation of further price declines, while demand in China remained muted. 
 Silver prices will also be closely tracked. Spot silver gained 1.2% to $49.6935 per ounce in early Asian trading on Monday. Platinum rose 0.8% to $1,446.05 per ounce, while palladium advanced 1.1% to $986.76. 
 Investors will monitor developments in the US-Iran conflict, inflation data, central bank commentary and expectations surrounding the Federal Reserve's next policy decision. The ongoing talks between Iranian negotiators and Qatari mediators in Doha could also influence market sentiment. 
 Follow this liveblog for the latest updates on domestic gold and silver rates, international bullion prices, market trends and expert views on what is driving the precious metals market. Live Events

Gold prices edged higher in early Asian trading but continued to hover near a one-year low, as persistent inflation concerns and growing expectations of a US Federal Reserve interest rate hike weighed on investor sentiment.
Spot gold rose 0.5% to $3,894.89 per ounce by 0042 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery gained 0.1% to $3,903.90. However, the yellow metal remained close to Friday's low, when it fell below the crucial $4,000-per-ounce mark.
The recent weakness has been driven by several factors, including rising inflation, hawkish comments from US Federal Reserve officials and expectations that borrowing costs could rise again in December. Traders are pricing in around a 75% probability of a rate hike, according to the CME FedWatch Tool. Higher interest rates tend to reduce the appeal of gold, which does not offer interest income.
The decline in global bullion prices has also been reflected in domestic markets. In New Delhi, gold of 99.9% purity fell by ₹3,200 to ₹1,42,000 per 10 grams on Saturday, its lowest level in 10 months. Silver prices dropped by ₹4,200 to ₹1,86,000 per kg.
Meanwhile, physical demand in India remained subdued last week, with buyers delaying purchases in anticipation of further price declines. Demand in China also remained muted.
Investors will track inflation trends, developments in the US-Iran conflict, central bank commentary and currency movements for fresh cues. Silver, which has also faced pressure from the broader precious metals sell-off, will remain under watch.
